gaps.sentence: I have no idea where he is — he ___ have gone to the gym, or maybe to the pool.
gaps.hint: an uncertain guess about the past
gaps.explanation: 'Might have' expresses an uncertain guess about the past: might have gone.

gaps.sentence: You ___ as well take the early train — the later one is often cancelled.
gaps.hint: might as well = no reason not to
gaps.explanation: 'Might as well' suggests an option because the alternative is worse.

gaps.sentence: I ___ help thinking he is hiding something.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't help' plus -ing means being unable to stop a feeling: can't help thinking.

gaps.sentence: We ___ book a table — the restaurant is never full on Mondays.
gaps.hint: the action is unnecessary, use needn't
gaps.explanation: When something is unnecessary, use 'needn't' or 'don't have to': needn't book.

gaps.sentence: Library books ___ be taken out of the reading room.
gaps.hint: a passive prohibition with mustn't be
gaps.explanation: Prohibitions can be passive: mustn't be taken.

gaps.sentence: There ___ be a supervisor present when students use the lab.
He ___ have driven so fast on that icy road — he is lucky to be unhurt.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' criticizes dangerous past behavior: shouldn't have.

gaps.sentence: Passengers ___ open the doors before the train stops completely.
gaps.hint: a safety rule that forbids something
